Yo coach, what does RPE 8 actually mean on heavy squats?

RPE 8 on heavy squats means "Rate of Perceived Exertion" of 8 out of 10. In practical terms, this represents having exactly 2 reps left in the tank. When you rack the barbell, you should be absolutely confident that you could have completed 2 more reps with solid technique before reaching muscular failure. The bar speed on the last rep will slow down slightly, but you should not be grinding or losing your spinal positioning. It is a heavy, challenging effort, but completely controlled and submaximal.

should I lock out my knees completely at the top of a leg press?

Absolutely not. You should never aggressively lock out your knees at the top of a leg press. Locking them out completely transfers the entire load of the machine off your quads and directly onto your joint capsule, meniscus, and ligaments. Where should the barbell touch my chest on a flat bench press? I want to make sure my shoulder alignment is absolutely locked in.

On a flat bench press, the barbell should touch your chest right around the lower sternum or the base of your breastbone (roughly in line with your nipples or slightly below them). Touching here allows your elbows to tuck naturally at about a 45-to-75-degree angle relative to your torso. This prevents your shoulders from flaring out excessively (at a 90-degree angle), which places immense shear stress on the subacromial space and rotator cuff. Focus on pulling your shoulder blades back and down into the bench, maintaining a solid shelf, and lowering the bar under control to that lower sternum touchpoint before driving up and back toward your face.

Yo coach, how wide should my grip be on lat pulldowns for max lat engagement? Everyone in my gym does it differently.

For maximum lat engagement, your grip on the lat pulldown bar should be just outside shoulder-width—roughly 1.5 times shoulder width. When you pull down, this grip width allows your forearms to remain vertical and perpendicular to the floor at the bottom of the movement, which directly aligns the pull with the orientation of your lat fibers. I keep seeing RPE 8 written on my heavy squat workouts. What does RPE 8 actually mean when I have a heavy barbell on my back?

RPE 8 (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on heavy squats means you finish a set with exactly 2 clean repetitions left in the tank. If you completed a set of 5 reps at RPE 8, it means that if your life depended on it, you could have grinded out a total of 7 reps, but you chose to stop at 5. The speed of your last rep will slow down noticeably, but you still maintain perfect technique without spinal flexion or your hips rising faster than your chest (the 'good morning' squat). It is a high-intensity threshold that stimulates serious strength and muscle growth while managing fatigue to ensure you can recover and smash your next session.

Explain RPE 8 to me for heavy squats. How do I know I'm actually hitting it and not sandbagging or overshooting?

To accurately gauge RPE 8 on heavy squats, you need to pay attention to your bar speed and mental reserves. An RPE 8 set should feel highly challenging, and the final rep will definitely slow down compared to your first rep. When you rack the bar, ask yourself: 'Could I have done two more reps with good form?' If the answer is a confident 'yes, but absolutely no more than two,' then you hit RPE 8. If you could only do one, you hit RPE 9. If you could have done three or more, you sandbagged and hit RPE 7. Tracking your sets on video is a great way to verify bar speed slowing down to confirm your rating.

How wide should my grip be on lat pulldowns for max lat engagement? Some bros tell me to go super wide, others say close grip.

For maximum lat engagement, skip the ultra-wide grip. A grip that is roughly 1.5 times your shoulder width—where your forearms are completely vertical at the bottom of the movement—is optimal. Going too wide limits your range of motion and forces your shoulders into a compromised position, shifting the load to your upper back. A slightly wider than shoulder-width grip allows you to drive your elbows straight down into your sides, which is the exact mechanical function of the lats. Keep your chest up and pull with your elbows, not your hands.

Where should the barbell touch my chest on a flat bench press? I keep touching near my collarbone and it feels super awkward.

Touching the barbell near your collarbone places extreme mechanical stress on your rotator cuffs and front delts. On a flat bench press, the bar should touch your lower chest/sternum, right around the nipple line or slightly below. This touchpoint allows you to keep your elbows tucked at a 45-to-60-degree angle relative to your torso. Tucking your elbows creates a stable structure, protects your shoulders, and maximizes chest and triceps mechanical tension. Keep your shoulder blades retracted and pinned down into the bench throughout the lift.

How do I breathe and brace on deadlifts? I feel like I lose my core tension right when I pull the bar off the floor.

To brace correctly for deadlifts, use the Valsalva maneuver. Before you pull, stand over the bar, take a deep belly breath (expand your stomach 360 degrees, not your chest), and then brace your core as if you're about to get punched in the stomach. Pack your lats by squeezing your armpits shut. Hold that breath and pressure throughout the entire concentric movement. Only exhale once you reach full lockout, or as you lower the bar. Re-brace from scratch at the bottom of every single rep; never bounce and pull without a reset.

What's the actual mechanical difference between RPE 9 and RPE 10 on a heavy lift? How do I know I hit failure?

RPE 10 is absolute maximum effort: you completed the final rep, but it was an extreme grind, and you could not physically complete a single additional rep or even half a rep. RPE 9 means you finished the set and could have completed exactly one more rep with decent form. True mechanical failure (RPE 10+) is when the muscle can no longer produce the force required to move the load through the concentric phase, causing the lift to stall completely despite maximum effort.

What is a good cue for a hip hinge? I keep squatting my RDLs instead of hinging.

The absolute best cue for a hip hinge is to pretend you are trying to close a car door with your butt while your hands are full. Stand a few inches from a wall, face away from it, and push your hips backward until your glutes touch the wall. Keep your shins completely vertical throughout the movement; your knees should bend slightly but never travel forward. If your knees shift forward, you are squatting. How do I generate proper leg drive on the bench press? My feet are just sliding around on the floor.

Leg drive on the bench press shouldn't push your hips off the bench; it should push your upper back *into* the bench. Place your feet flat on the floor and pull them back slightly toward your hips until your quads are tight. Squeeze your glutes. When you press the bar off your chest, drive your heels into the floor as if you are trying to slide your body off the top of the bench. If your feet are sliding, you need grippy shoes or to plant your feet firmly. Keep your core tight to transfer that leg force up to your chest.

Should I go all the way down to my chest on incline dumbbell presses or stop at 90 degrees?

For maximum chest hypertrophy, you should press through a full range of motion, which means letting the dumbbells descend until they are right next to your upper chest. Research shows that training muscles at long muscle lengths (in the deep stretch position) yields superior muscle growth compared to partial range reps. Stopping at 90 degrees of elbow flexion cuts out the most hypertrophic part of the movement. If you experience shoulder pain in the deep stretch, tuck your elbows in slightly to a 45-degree angle rather than flaring them out.

What is the best bar path for the bench press? Should the bar travel in a straight line up and down?

No, a straight vertical line is actually an inefficient bar path for the bench press. The optimal bar path is a slight diagonal J-curve. The bar starts directly over your shoulders at lockout, descends down and forward to touch your lower chest/upper sternum, and then travels back and up in a curved path to lockout directly over your joints again. Pressing in a straight vertical line from your chest puts excessive stress on your shoulders and prevents you from fully engaging your chest and triceps mechanical leverage.

Should I lock out my knees completely at the top of a leg press, or should I keep a slight bend?

Keep a very slight bend (soft knees) at the top of a leg press. You should never hyperextend or micro-bounce at terminal extension under load, as this shifts the massive mechanical load off your quadriceps and directly onto your cruciate ligaments, menisci, and joint capsules. Focus on halting the movement 1-2 degrees before soft lockout to maintain constant metabolic tension on your quads and protect your knees.

What does RPE 8 actually mean on heavy barbell squats? How do I know I'm not sandbagging?

RPE 8 (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on heavy squats means you have exactly 2 clean reps left in the tank (2 RIR) before mechanical failure occurs. To ensure you aren't sandbagging, watch your bar velocity. On heavy squats, an RPE 8 rep is where the bar noticeably slows down through your sticking point, but you can still push through it with clean form and without grinding to a near-halt. If the bar is still flying up, you're likely at RPE 6-7.

How wide should my grip be on lat pulldowns for max lat engagement? Everyone at my gym tells me different things.

For maximum lat hypertrophy, your grip should be roughly 1.2 to 1.5 times shoulder-width. You do not want a super-wide grip; that limits your range of motion and forces more scapular adduction (upper back/terez major) rather than lat adduction. A moderate grip allows you to pull your elbows straight down into your sides, achieving a full lat stretch at the top and maximum contraction in deep shoulder extension.

Should I touch the bar to my chest on every single rep of bench press, or is it cool to stop an inch short?

For maximum hypertrophy and muscle recruitment, touch the bar to your chest on every rep, provided you have the shoulder mobility to do so pain-free. Stopping an inch short misses the maximum weighted stretch of the pectoralis fibers in deep extension, which is the most anabolic portion of the lift. However, if you have a structural shoulder issue, stopping an inch high can be a valid modification, but for healthy lifters, full range of motion is superior.

When I am doing RPE 9 sets on deadlifts, my upper back rounds slightly. Is this safe or is my spine going to explode?

Slight upper back rounding (thoracic flexion) at RPE 9 is actually a common and safe biomechanical trade-off used by advanced lifters to pull heavier weights. It shortens the lever arm between the bar and your hips, making the lift mechanically easier. The crucial caveat: your lower back (lumbar spine) MUST remain completely locked in neutral. If your lumbar spine is rounding under that RPE 9 load, you are risking a severe disc herniation.

Where should my elbows be pointing during dumbbell flat bench press? Out to the sides or tucked in?

Your elbows should be tucked at roughly a 45-degree angle relative to your torso. Flare them out to 90 degrees and you put extreme shear stress on your rotator cuffs and subacromial space. Tuck them too close (0 degrees) and you turn it into a tricep-dominant close-grip press. A 45-to-60-degree flare represents the biomechanical sweet spot for maximum chest fiber alignment and joint safety.

What's the difference between RIR 1 and RIR 3 on bicep curls? How do I gauge the intensity?

At RIR 1 (1 Rep in Reserve), bicep curls are incredibly slow, your forearms are burning, and you have to fight hard with absolute muscular concentration to get the barbell past the sticking point without swaying. At RIR 3, you are still moving the weight with solid velocity and could comfortably knock out three more reps without losing form or feeling extreme burning. Gauge your sets by tracking when your concentric speed drops.

When doing barbell rows, should my torso be completely parallel to the floor or can I stand up slightly?

Your torso should be angled between parallel and 15 degrees above parallel. A strict parallel position maximizes lat and lower back work, but can limit the weight you can handle. Standing up slightly (around 15-30 degrees) allows for heavier loading on the lats and rhomboids, but standing up too high (45+ degrees) transforms it into an upright row/shrug, focusing tension on the upper traps instead.

How do I breathe properly on heavy deadlifts? Do I inhale on the way up or before?

On heavy deadlifts, you should use the Valsalva maneuver to stabilize your spine. Take a massive, 360-degree diaphragmatic breath before you pull, while you are standing or in the setup. Tighten your abdominal wall as if you are about to be punched in the stomach. Hold that breath and brace through the entire lift, only exhaling once you have locked out the weight or successfully completed the descent.

Coach, what does RPE 8 actually mean on heavy squats? How do I know I'm there?

RPE 8 (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on heavy squats means you have exactly 2 repetitions left in the tank. When you rack the barbell, you should feel 100% confident you could have performed 2 more clean reps with consistent form. Bar speed will slow down slightly on the final rep, but it won't be an absolute, shaky grind where your hips rise faster than the bar or your knees cave. It's a heavy, focused effort, but safe.

Should I lock out my knees completely at the top of a leg press, or should I keep them slightly bent?

Never lock out your knees completely at the top of a leg press. Joint lockout under heavy load transfers the weight from your quads and glutes directly onto your knee joints and meniscus, which can cause severe hyperextension injuries. Stop each rep just short of absolute lockout (about a 1-to-2 degree bend). This maintains continuous tension on your quadriceps and keeps your joints perfectly safe.

Where should the barbell touch my chest on a flat bench press? I feel like I am too high up near my neck.

The barbell should touch your chest at your lower sternum, which is roughly right in line with your nipples. Touching near your neck or clavicle flares your elbows to a dangerous 90-degree angle, placing massive shear force on your rotator cuffs. Keep your shoulders packed down, tuck your elbows at roughly a 45-to-60 degree angle on the descent, and aim for that mid-to-lower sternum touchpoint.

How do I cue my lats on a barbell row? I feel like my biceps are taking over the whole movement.

To engage your lats and keep your biceps from taking over your barbell rows, use the 'elbow pull' cue. Instead of thinking about pulling the bar up with your hands, imagine your hands are just hooks. Focus on driving your elbows back and up toward your hips. Initiate the pull by squeezing your shoulder blades together, and pull the bar toward your belly button rather than your chest. This mechanical path maximizes lat engagement.

What is the actual difference between RPE 9 and RPE 10 on a set of dumbbell curls?

On a set of dumbbell curls, RPE 9 means you have exactly 1 clean rep left in the tank. If you absolute pushed it, you could get one more up with a slight grind. RPE 10 is absolute muscular failure. It means you could not perform another full rep even if someone offered you a million dollars. If you attempted another rep, the weight would stop halfway up the movement, and your muscle would lock up. RPE 10 is maximum intensity.

Proper bracing is crucial for deadlifts. Before you pull, stand over the bar, take a deep 360-degree belly breath (filling your abdomen, not your chest), and brace your core as if you're about to get punched in the stomach. What is the difference between RIR (Reps in Reserve) and RPE? They sound exactly the same.

They are two sides of the same coin. RIR (Reps in Reserve) counts how many reps you have left before reaching complete muscular failure. RPE (Rate of Perceived Exertion) is a scale from 1 to 10 that rates your effort. They correlate directly: an RIR of 2 is an RPE of 8 (meaning you had 2 reps left). An RIR of 1 is an RPE of 9 (1 rep left). RIR is often easier to track because it is a direct countdown of your physical capability.

Should my elbows be flared out or tucked on the flat bench press?

This safe position optimizes chest, shoulder, and tricep contribution while protecting your joints.

Yo coach, should I lock out my knees completely at the top of a leg press?

Absolutely not, my friend. Under no circumstances should you lock out your knees aggressively at the top of a leg press. Keeping a soft lock (about 1-2 degrees short of terminal extension) does two critical things: first, it keeps the mechanical tension directly on your quadriceps rather than transferring the load entirely onto your knee joints, ACL, and patellar structures; second, it prevents catastrophic hyperextension under heavy loading. Keep that tension on the muscle, not the joint, and control the eccentric.

Hey, what does RPE 8 actually mean on heavy squats?

RPE 8 (Rate of Perceived Exertion) on heavy squats means you finish the set with exactly 2 reps left in the tank (2 RIR - Reps in Reserve). This means if you rack the bar on rep 5, you are 100% confident you could have squeezed out a 6th and 7th rep with solid, acceptable form, but a 8th rep would have resulted in technical breakdown or absolute muscle failure. It's the sweet spot for heavy compound progression because it drives massive mechanical tension without completely frying your recovery and central nervous system.

How wide should my grip be on lat pulldowns for max lat engagement?

For maximum lat engagement, skip the ultra-wide grip. You want a grip that is just slightly wider than shoulder-width—roughly 1.5 times shoulder width. This setup ensures that at the bottom of the movement, your forearms are completely vertical and perpendicular to the floor. An ultra-wide grip limits your range of motion and forces more contribution from your teres major and upper upper back, whereas a slightly narrower, shoulder-width or semi-wide grip allows you to drive your elbows fully into your pockets for a complete, maximum contraction of the lower lat fibers.

Is it okay if my heels lift slightly off the ground during back squats?

No, your heels lifting during a back squat is a major biomechanical red flag. When your heels rise, your center of mass shifts forward, throwing the load onto your toes and placing excessive shear stress on your knees and patellar tendons. This is usually caused by poor ankle dorsiflexion mobility or tight calves. To fix this instantly, try widening your stance slightly, flare your toes out to 15-30 degrees, or slide dynamic weightlifting shoes (with an elevated heel) on. Keep your foot flat and drive through the mid-foot.

Coach, how do I apply RPE to my accessory work like dumbbell lateral raises?

Applying RPE to isolation accessory movements like lateral raises is a bit different than on big compounds. For accessory work, you should aim for higher RPE ranges (RPE 9 to 10) because the systemic recovery cost is extremely low. Since you're not risking spinal loading, push these sets right to the limit. Use a weight where RPE 9 (1 rep in reserve) is hit around the 12-15 rep range, and focus strictly on keeping the traps out of the movement and maintaining strict eccentric control rather than just slinging the weight up.

Should I keep my shoulder blades retracted during the entire bench press movement?

Yes, absolutely. Keeping your scapulae retracted (squeezed together) and depressed (pulled down into your back pockets) throughout the entire bench press is crucial. This creates a stable, solid foundation against the bench, maximizes pectoral stretch at the bottom, and drastically reduces subacromial wear-and-tear on your rotator cuffs. Do not let your shoulders roll forward at the top lockout phase; keep that chest up and shoulder blades locked tight.

Yo coach, how do I find my optimal foot stance width for conventional deadlifts?

A great rule of thumb to find your optimal conventional deadlift stance is to perform a vertical jump. Look down at where your feet naturally land—that jump-width stance (typically hip-width apart) is usually your strongest, most anatomically efficient position for vertical power transfer. Your hands should then grip the bar just outside of your legs without pushing your knees inward. This setup keeps your hips high and leverages your posterior chain perfectly.

What's the difference between RPE 9 and actual muscle failure on bicep curls?

On bicep curls, RPE 9 means you complete a rep with high effort, and you are completely certain you could only do exactly one more rep with strict form before your muscles lock up. Absolute muscle failure (RPE 10) means you literally cannot complete the concentric (upward) portion of the curl, even if you put every ounce of effort into it. For hypertrophy, hitting RPE 9-10 on biceps is highly effective, but make sure you aren't using momentum or lower back swing to cheat your way to an artificial RPE.

How low should I go on dumbbell incline press to get max chest stretch without risking injury?

To get a safe, maximal chest stretch on an incline dumbbell press, lower the dumbbells until the inside bell of the dumbbell is roughly level with your mid-to-upper chest. Your elbows should be tucked at about a 45-to-60 degree angle relative to your torso—never flared out at 90 degrees, which shreds your rotator cuffs. Going deeper than chest level isn't necessary and places excess strain on the anterior shoulder capsule. Focus on a controlled 2-second negative to feel the stretch safely.

Should I be using a thumbless grip on pull-ups to target my lats better?

Using a thumbless grip (or 'suicide grip') is actually an excellent cue for better lat isolation on pull-ups. By removing your thumb from wrapping around the bar, you mentally shift the mechanical focus from 'squeezing and pulling with your hands' to 'pulling down through your elbows'. Think of your hands as simple hooks. This reduces over-activation of the forearms and biceps, allowing you to recruit the lats much more effectively at the initiation of the pull.

Mechanically, this means if you absolute-failed or hit muscular collapse on rep 10, your RPE 8 set ended at rep 8. Where exactly should the barbell touch my chest on a flat bench press? I feel like I'm hitting too high up near my neck.

On a flat bench press, the barbell should touch your lower chest/sternum—typically right around your nipples or slightly below them (mid-to-low sternum). This naturally guides the barbell down in a slight J-curve path, landing perfectly on your lower sternum for a strong, shoulder-safe pressing position.

Should I be using a thumbless grip (suicide grip) on overhead press, or is it better to wrap my thumb?

What's the difference between RPE 9 and RPE 10? I find it hard to tell when I've actually hit absolute failure.
